transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rita Kumar (CTO, Helix Data), Samir Patel (ML Engineer), Lena Ortiz (Platform Engineer)

Summary: quick poc scoping focused on integration approach: reuse OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDKs (Python/Node), function/tool calling for structured outputs. Discussed success criteria (latency, cost, quality), workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, and security/network constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Next: Redwood to run benchmark, send pricing and security docs, schedule infra deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Diego our SE.
[00:07] Rita (Helix): Hey, Rita here, CTO at Helix Data. we've got Samir and Lena on the call.
[00:11] Samir: hi all.
[00:13] Diego (Redwood SE): morning. ok the agenda -- POC success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and then integration details around SDKs and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, plus function calling for structured outputs.
[00:25] Lena: sounds good, we're particularly interested in minimizing changes to our current integration we use with OpenAI today.
[00:30] Maya: perfect. high level - Helix wants to evaluate Redwood for conversational agents + document understanding in the POC correct?
[00:36] Rita: yes. primary goals are: 1) get quality equal/greater than current, 2) meet latency SLOs for our UI, and 3) validate cost per request.
[00:44] Diego: good. can you give us numbers for traffic and payloads? sample sizes?
[00:48] Samir: sure - daily active users for the feature are ~12k, but for the POC we expect to run a smaller trial: ~1k DAU, with peaks around 25 RPS. typical prompt length 80-150 tokens, generation target ~150-300 tokens for summaries. We also have a few long-form runs up to 800 tokens for batch summarization.
[01:10] Diego: ok so for the POC we can plan for a baseline of 30 RPS to be safe. latency target? what does your UI need at 95th?
[01:18] Rita: 95th < 300ms for the interactive UI. batch jobs can be higher.
[01:24] Maya: noted. quality success criteria? any specific metrics - Rouge/F1? or human-annotated pass/fail?
[01:30] Samir: we have a small eval set - about 100 golden prompts with expected structured JSON outputs and scoring script. pass if > 85% on our rubric. also need stable structured outputs for downstream ingestion, so function/tool-calling support or consistent JSON output is important.
[01:43] Diego: Redwood supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints so you can point existing SDK calls to us with minimal changes. We also have our Python/Node SDKs, and function-calling compatibility layered on top. For structured outputs we recommend using the function-calling interface or our structured output templates which help reduce hallucinations.
[01:58] Lena: can you clarify "OpenAI-compatible" - do we have to change auth headers or anything?
[02:03] Diego: minimal. same API shape: model param, messages, streaming, etc. auth token header is similar; our SDKs wrap that and handle retries & batching. For example, your current code that calls chat.completions should translate with only a base url change and minor param rename in a couple spots.
[02:18] Samir: and for function calls - will the behavior be identical? we rely on deterministic JSON outputs from function calling to write to downstream services.
[02:25] Diego: behavior is very similar, but we do have platform-level options: you can enable "strict schema enforcement" which will attempt to coerce outputs to your schema and surface errors. it's not perfect but reduces manual postprocessing. We'll include that in the benchmark run.
[02:39] Rita: cool. about benchmarks - we want latency (p50/p95), throughput, and cost per 1k requests. can you run that against our 100 sample prompts?
[02:47] Maya: yes, Diego can run a perf job if you share the prompt set and a few sample contexts. Diego, plan?
[02:52] Diego: I'll run two profiles: Hosted Redwood API on our standard curated model, and Dedicated (reserved) with a quantized variant. We'll measure p50/p95 with 30 RPS sustained and a 100-concurrent short-test to simulate spikes, and also run the long-form 800-token job as a batch.
[03:08] Samir: what's the expected latency delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[03:12] Diego: Hosted is optimized for multi-tenant low-latency, you might see ~150-300ms p95 on the short prompts depending on model and sequence length. Dedicated with pinned capacity and HW at parity can get you lower p95 and more consistent tail - maybe 20-30% improvement for same model family, plus better cost predictability. we'll include actual numbers.
[03:33] Maya: and we'll provide a simple cost model: tokens per request * token price + allocation cost for dedicated. we'll put that in the spreadsheet.
[03:40] Lena: security - important for us. we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and we prefer VPC peering for Dedicated. do you support KMS and customer-managed keys?
[03:49] Diego: yes to SOC2 and SAML; we also support KMS integrations for Private deployments and Dedicated can be configured behind VPC peering for network isolation. For hosted API we provide data controls and configurable retention but for strict compliance you'd look at Private deployment. We'll share the SOC2 report and a VPC peering checklist.
[04:07] Rita: any requirements on egress from our network? Our security team may block outbound to non-whitelisted endpoints.
[04:12] Lena: yep, that's likely.
[04:13] Diego: if egress is blocked we can support Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering so traffic stays within allowed paths. We'll document ports and IP ranges.
[04:24] Samir: integration-wise we want to reuse our OpenAI wrappers; minimal changes is key. can you handle streaming responses and partial tokens (we rely on immediate UI streaming)?
[04:33] Diego: yes, streaming is supported. our streaming endpoints use the same chunked behavior; sometimes the event names are slightly different in the SDK but the overall flow is the same.
[04:41] Maya: timelines - what would a POC look like? typical is 2-4 weeks for an initial integration and evaluation.
[04:47] Rita: we were thinking 3 weeks. week 1: integration and sample runs, week 2: perf benchmark and quality eval, week 3: decision and next steps.
[04:55] Diego: that works. immediate tasks: Helix to share prompt set + schemas; Redwood to run perf and share spreadsheet + pricing. After perf we can do a deep-dive on network/VPC details if needed.
[05:06] Samir: about structured outputs - if function calling fails or hallucinates, how do you surface the errors? we want deterministic failures to avoid bad writes to downstream stores.
[05:15] Diego: we can enable schema enforcement and a pre-commit validation step: the API can return a validation status with the response. You can also supply our SDK a postprocess hook. We'll show examples in the sample integration repo.
[05:25] Rita: do you have example code for converting current OpenAI calls to Redwood? even a checklist would be useful.
[05:31] Maya: yes we'll share a migration guide + a small repo with Python and Node samples showing base_url swaps, auth examples, function call wiring, and streaming.
[05:40] Lena: one more on observability - do you expose per-request token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards? Our SRE wants tracing correlation IDs.
[05:47] Diego: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency, per-model dashboards, and you can pass a trace id that gets surfaced in logs. For Dedicated/Private we can also forward logs into your Splunk/Datadog via hooks.
[05:58] Samir: any limits or rate limiting that might affect our bursty traffic?
[06:02] Maya: for POC we'll provision higher rate limits and can set policy to throttle gracefully. for production we'll size dedicated capacity or autoscaling policies.
[06:10] Rita: ok, sounds pragmatic. any blockers from your side or must-have items for us?
[06:15] Samir: need the sample prompts and the scoring script; also confirmation of retention policy and deletion options for hosted.
[06:21] Diego: we'll include retention settings, plus a paper trail for deletion APIs.
[06:25] Maya: recap of next steps — Diego runs benchmark once Samir and Rita share the 100 prompts and scoring script; Maya sends pricing and migration guide + security docs; schedule infra deep-dive.
[06:36] Rita: perfect. thanks all.
[06:39] Maya: we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive and send the artifacts.
[06:43] Lena: thanks, bye.
[06:44] Samir: thanks.

Notes & references:
- Referenced artifacts to be shared via email/link: 1) Helix 100-prompt eval set and scoring script (customer), 2) Redwood perf/cost spreadsheet (to be provided), 3) Redwood SOC2 + VPC peering checklist (to be provided).
